title: First and last N countries
description:
Write a function `first_and_last_n(path, n)` that reads the country data JSON file at `path` and returns `(first_n_names, last_n_names)`.

Covers source items 14-15 (first ten countries, last ten countries) as one exercise - both are slicing the same loaded list from opposite ends.
starter_code:
import json


def first_and_last_n(path, n):
    # your code here
    pass
hints: Idea to consider: slicing from the front and from the back
names[:n] takes the first n items; names[-n:] takes the last n - the same slice syntax, just anchored at opposite ends of the list.
Load the file, extract every country's name into one list, and return (names[:n], names[-n:]).
expected_behavior: Returns the first n and last n country names as a tuple of two lists.

hidden_tests.expected: (['Afghanistan', 'Åland Islands', 'Albania', 'Algeria', 'American Samoa', 'Andorra', 'Angola', 'Anguilla', 'Antarctica', 'Antigua and Barbuda'], ['Uruguay', 'Uzbekistan', 'Vanuatu', 'Venezuela (Bolivarian Republic of)', 'Viet Nam', 'Wallis and Futuna', 'Western Sahara', 'Yemen', 'Zambia', 'Zimbabwe'])
hidden_tests.label: source items 14-15

solution:
import json


def first_and_last_n(path, n):
    with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
        countries = json.load(f)
    names = [c["name"] for c in countries]
    return names[:n], names[-n:]
explanation: names[:n] and names[-n:] are the same slicing tool used throughout this correction (Day 4's char_at, Day 10's reverse_list) - only the position of the slice changes.
